title: Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Managed Services en Consultancy voor de ServiceNow Omgeving
description: LVNL wenst één geschikte dienstverlener te selecteren die LVNL zelfstandig en langdurig kan ondersteunen bij het beheer, onderhoud en de doorontwikkeling van het ServiceNow-platform, inclusief de daarop gebaseerde modules, scoped applicaties en integraties. De nadruk ligt op het waarborgen van continuïteit, beschikbaarheid, kwaliteit, veiligheid en toekomstbestendigheid van het platform. De dienstverlener levert hiervoor specialistische ondersteuningsdiensten in de vorm van Managed Services voor beheer en Consultancy voor doorontwikkeling. Van de leverancier wordt verwacht dat deze optreedt als strategische en uitvoerende ServiceNow-partner voor LVNL. De leverancier levert technisch applicatiebeheer, ondersteunt bij lifecycle management en upgrades, voert configuratiewijzigingen uit, adviseert over platformontwikkeling en licentiegebruik en ondersteunt LVNL bij wijzigingen, uitbreidingen en implementatie van nieuwe functionaliteit. Zie de Offerteleidraad voor de volledige omschrijving. Binnen LVNL wordt ServiceNow gebruikt als strategisch platform voor IT Service Management (ITSM) en de ondersteuning van diverse bedrijfsprocessen. Naast de standaard ServiceNow-functionaliteit zijn op het platform aanvullende applicaties ontwikkeld, waaronder EWR. Het platform wordt beheerd door LVNL, ondersteund door een externe specialistische ServiceNow-partner. LVNL wenst een duurzame samenwerking aan te gaan met één leverancier die het beheer, de ondersteuning en de doorontwikkeling van het platform kan verzorgen. De gewenste dienstverlening bestaat in hoofdlijn uit twee diensten, te weten Managed Services (Beheer) en Consultancy. De overeenkomst treedt naar verwachting in werking medio februari 2027. De overeenkomst heeft een initiële looptijd van 2 jaar met viermaal een optie op een verlenging van 2 jaar. De totale maximale looptijd van de overeenkomst bedraagt 10 jaar. Voor een volledige omschrijving wordt hier verwezen naar de Offerteleidraad voor deze aanbesteding.

title: Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade
description: DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HQ04022_88127 – Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade, Gagetown, NB DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HQ04022_88127 – Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade, Gagetown, NB Defence Construction Canada (DCC) invites general contractors to express their interest in providing all labour, materials, and equipment necessary for the Enniskillen Road Upgrade at Gagetown, NB This Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) is the first step of a two-step solicitation process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only general contractors that have expressed their interest through the Electronic Bidding System prior to the closing date and time of this RFEOI will be invited to submit a proposal at the second stage. Only submissions received in accordance with the requirements of the Electronic Bidding System will be considered. Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase. DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI. As part of Canada’s commitment to maximize the participation of Indigenous Businesses, bidders are advised that this solicitation includes an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP). The Contractor will have to include Indigenous businesses (or eligible joint ventures) as subcontractors or suppliers to this project. Further details will be provided in the Tender phase. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). Project background A detailed project background can be reviewed in the Building Summary Documents Technical plans and specifications are not available during this RFEOI and will be provided during the Tender Phase; however, the Standard Construction Contract Documents for Electronic Bidding, DCL 250E, are available on DCC's website: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. Tenderers are advised that this contract is subject to DCC's Procurement Code of Conduct, which can be downloaded at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or supplier who has been declared ineligible or suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and whose period of ineligibility or suspension may not have expired will not be able to proceed to the second stage. Bid security will be required during the Tender Phase in accordance with DCL193E- Instructions for Bidders for Electronic Bidding item 5. Estimate The Rough Order Magnitude estimate / Construction Cost Limit for this Contract is $ 25,642,471.00. This amount includes all construction costs, on-site work (including all required services, parking, and landscaping), site utilities, necessary redundant mechanical systems, communication conduits and wiring, backup power equipment, built-in equipment, built-in furniture, and inflation to achieve substantial completion. This amount excludes HST, design costs, travel and disbursements, consultant fees and expenses, movable equipment and furniture, IT equipment and contingencies. Schedule DCC will proceed with the Tender Phase around November - December 2026. The works shall reach substantial completion no later than October 15, 2027 and shall be completed no later than November 15, 2027.\ Site visit No site visits will be offered during the RFEOI however, during the Tender Phase, bidders will be invited to a site visit. Access to information Act Tenderers are advised that DCC is subject to the provisions of the Access to Information Act (Canada). Information submitted may be eligible for disclosure in accordance with the requirements of the Act. Questions and clarifications Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted in writing to DCC's Coordinator, Contract Services whose contact information can be found in the Electronic Bid System. DCC reserves the right to request clarification and/or confirmation regarding any aspect of this RFEOI to the Tenderer. In such a case, the Coordinator, Contract Services will be responsible for making the request. The request for clarification and/or confirmation will be sent to the contact person identified on the Electronic Submission System. Language of the Tender and the contract By submitting a response to this RFEOI, Tenderers will be invited to choose the desired official language for the tender documents and any resulting contract. In the Tender Phase, tender documents will be published in the language chosen by the Tenderer in the Electronic Bid System. Unless otherwise specified in the Contract, all Contract Documents to which the Contract applies or refers, as well as all deliverables, documents, reports and results of the work, services or goods that the Contractor submits, provides, or delivers to DCC or Canada in connection with the performance of the Contract, shall be in the language chosen by the Contractor on the Electronic Bid System. Joint venture A joint venture is an association of two or more parties that pools their funds, assets, knowledge, expertise, or other resources into a joint business venture, sometimes called a consortium, to bid together for a requirement. Tenderers submitting interest as a joint venture will be required to clearly indicate in the Electronic Submission System that they are forming a joint venture and should provide the following information: the name of the joint venture, if applicable, the name of the representative of the joint venture, i.e., the member chosen by the other members to represent them, if applicable, the name of each member of the joint venture. Closing location Responses to this RFEOI must be received through the Electronic Bidding System.  Responses sent by fax, mail or email will not be accepted.  Closing Date and Time The closing date and time indicated in the Electronic Submission System will be the official closing date and time of this RFEOI.      Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

Osoite on Vermonpolku 3, Espoo. Kohde käsittää yhden 3-kerroksisen luhtitalon ja kolme 2-kerroksista rivitaloa talousrakennuksineen ja pihoineen. Autopaikat sijoitetaan tontille maantasopaikoituksena urakkaan kuuluvina. Kaavan sallima kokonaisrakennusoikeus on 2600 k-m2, jakautuen kerrostaloon (1300 k-m2) ja rivitaloihin (yht. 1300 k-m2). Tavoitteellisen tilaohjelman mukainen asuntojen huoneistoala on yhteensä 2228,5 m2 ja asuntojen lukumäärä on 45 kappaletta, jolloin autopaikkamäärä on 24 kappaletta.

buyer: Stadt Chur - Immobilien und Bewirtschaftung, Facility Services
title: Stadt Chur - Prestations de planification et de déménagement pour les environnements de travail de bureau
description:
La Ville de Coire a pour objectif de développer ses sites administratifs en fonction des besoins, de manière économique et tournée vers l’avenir. Les environnements de travail modernes doivent favoriser la collaboration, soutenir différentes formes de travail et offrir au personnel un cadre de travail contemporain. Parallèlement, les exigences en matière de flexibilité, d’efficacité de l’utilisation des surfaces, de durabilité et d’orientation vers les utilisateurs n’ont cessé d’augmenter ces dernières années.

La planification et le développement des environnements de travail de bureau comprennent aussi bien des tâches de planification et de conception que la réalisation des déménagements, des réorganisations et des modifications de postes de travail qui y sont liés. Ces prestations nécessitent différentes compétences spécialisées ainsi qu’une collaboration coordonnée entre la planification et la mise en œuvre opérationnelle.

Afin de réaliser les projets correspondants, la Ville de Coire entend donc mandater des prestataires externes qualifiés pour la planification des postes de travail ainsi que pour l’exécution opérationnelle des déménagements.

Le présent appel d’offres porte sur la conclusion d’accords-cadres pour des prestations de planification et de déménagement liées aux environnements de travail de bureau. L’objectif est de permettre à la Ville de Coire de faire appel, en fonction de ses besoins, à des partenaires spécialisés qualifiés pour ses futurs projets et de planifier et réaliser ceux-ci de manière efficace, cohérente et avec un niveau de qualité garanti.

description: L’objet de l'accord cadre porte sur la fourniture d’instruments météorologiques et prestations associées au profit des centres appartenant à la Direction de l’Ingénierie et de l’Expertise (DIE) de direction générale de l’armement. Il s'agit d'un accord­-cadre composite mono­-attributaire, composé de deux parties : Une part à bons de commande conformément aux dispositions de l’article R.2362-8 au Code de la Commande Publique (CCP) et une part à marchés subséquents conformément aux articles R.2362-1 à R.2362-7 du CCP. Pour la part à bons de commandes : la fourniture, l’installation, la mise en service et formation et d’instruments météorologiques et leur maintien en condition opérationnelle Les prestations qui pourront être réalisées dans le cadre de ce présent projet d’accord­-cadre sont notamment : Famille 1: Mesure de la température. Famille 2 : Mesure de la pression atmosphérique. Famille 3 : Mesure de l’humidité, Famille 4 : Mesure du vent en surface Famille 5 : Mesure des précipitations Famille 6 : Mesure du rayonnement Famille 7 : Mesure de la visibilité Famille 8 : Observation du temps présent et passé et de l’état du sol, Famille 9 : Observation et mesure des propriétés des nuages Famille 10 : Accessoires Les marchés subséquents préciseront certaines prestations ou fournitures ultérieures, dont les caractéristiques et les modalités d’exécution sont non définies dans l’accord-cadre. Les prestations seront réalisées au profit de : DGA Essais de missiles Site Gironde : Saint¬ Médard en­ Jalles (33), DGA Essais de missiles Site Landes : Biscarrosse (40),DGA Essais de missiles Site Méditerranée Toulon, Levant et Coudon (83), DGA Techniques navales Site de Toulon (83), DGA Techniques navales Site de Brest (29), DGA Essais de missiles Bâtiment d’Essais et de Mesures Monge, DGA Essais de missiles Station d’Essais et de Mesures de Quimper (29), DGA Essais de missiles Station d'Essais de Mesures d'Hourtin (SEMH) (33), DGA Essais propulseurs : Saclay (91), DGA Maîtrise de l'information : Bruz (35), DGA Essais en vol Site de Cazaux (33), DGA Essais en vol Site d’Istres (13), DGA Maîtrise NRBC : Vert Le Petit (91), DGA Techniques aérospatiales : Balma (31), DGA Techniques hydrodynamiques : Val de Reuil (27), DGA Techniques terrestres Site de Bourges (18), DGA Techniques terrestres Site d’Angers (49). La date limite de remise des candidatures est fixée au 12/11/2026 à 16:00 heures (Heure de Paris). La date et l'heure limites inscrites à la rubrique 5.1.12 sont au format UTC. Il s'agit d'un Marché de défense ou de sécurité. Le présent projet de marché fait l'objet d'une procédure formalisée négociée avec mise en concurrence et publicité préalable, conformément aux dispositions des articles L.2324-1, L.2324-3, R.2324-1, R.2324-3, et R.2361-8 à R.2361-12 du CCP. L'accord-­cadre est conclu pour une durée de validité de 7 (sept) ans. Le montant maximum s'élève à 7 000 000 € HT, indiqués à la rubrique 2.1.3 ci­-après. Ce montant maximum correspond à une estimation globale pour le projet d'accord­-cadre, sans engagement de la part de l'État de l'atteindre. Le montant maximum indiqué en rubriques 2 et 5 ci-après est en euros hors taxe. Les candidats doivent indiquer dans leur candidature s'ils se présentent en tant que candidat individuel ou groupement d'opérateurs économiques. Il est interdit aux candidats de présenter pour l'accord­-cadre plusieurs offres en agissant à la fois : 1. en qualité de candidats individuels et de membres d'un ou plusieurs groupements ; 2. en qualité de membres de plusieurs groupements. La forme du groupement n'est pas imposée. La composition des groupements peut être modifiée, et il est possible d'en constituer de nouveaux entre la remise des candidatures et la remise des offres initiales si tous les membres du nouveau groupement, présenté au stade des offres, ont été autorisés au stade des candidatures à présenter une offre ou à y participer, au moins en tant que sous-contractant accepté dans la phase candidature. Le groupement nouvellement constitué doit respecter les exigences relatives aux capacités des candidats. De plus, les dispositions des articles R.2142-23 et R.2342-14 du CCP s’appliquent. La fourniture de tous les éléments/documents listés en rubriques 2.1.6 et 5.1.9 est primordiale, sous peine de rejet de la candidature de l’opérateur économique. Le présent avis de marché ne concerne que la PHASE CANDIDATURE. Le dossier de consultation sera envoyé ultérieurement aux candidats admis à soumissionner. Il pourra être fait application des dispositions de l'article R.2394-1 du CCP (clauses de réexamen relative aux conditions de variation des prix, à des évolutions, aux références des instruments de météorologie, aux situations de crise et rajout de sites bénéficiaires).

title: Ireland – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – R232 Glenmore Bridge Widening and Road Realignment Scheme
description: Donegal County Council proposes to upgrade the section of the existing R232 that crosses Lough Ultan River at Glenmore approx. 4.7km West of Pettigo. The proposed road will provide an improved alignment and cross section. The project will include: a) A new concrete extension to the existing masonry bridge crossing the Lough Ultan River on the realigned R232. b) The realignment of approximately 0.7km of road infrastructure and cross-sectional improvements. Works will include, but are not limited to, the following: - Earthworks including excavation and filling and the disposal of surplus material; - Overhead telecom service diversion; - Drainage works; - Pavement construction; - Works on and adjacent to live carriageways along a narrow and winding alignment; - Works adjacent to woodland; - Works on and adjacent to the existing watercourse, including temporary diversion (piping); - Works on and adjacent to the existing bridge structure, including partial removal of wingwalls, repair and repointing to the bridge stonework; - Traffic management including temporary traffic routing to keep the Regional Road open; - In-situ concrete construction of bridge extension components; - Fabrication and erection of precast arch bridge elements; - Safety barriers, timber post fencing; - Tie-ins to the existing road at either end; - Tie-ins with a number of farm accesses.

title: Incubator Programs for Secure Facilities and Networks at Universities
description: Pursuant to Section 1071 of Public Law 119-60, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Section 1071), the Department of War (DoW) is conducting an assessment on the feasibility, advisability, and potential benefits of establishing incubator programs for the development, operation, and sustainment of secure facilities and networks at select institutions of higher education. This RFI seeks detailed information from institutions capable of: Establishing or expanding secure facilities and networks Accelerating the transition of innovative technologies to DoW mission use Increasing availability of secure spaces to support classified research and development (R&D), prototyping, secure collaboration, and research transition activities Expanding the cleared technical workforce Serving as a regional innovation hub supporting multi-tenant use (DoW, industry, and academia) Long-term economic sustainment with significant non-federal cost-sharing The Department intends to use RFI responses to inform its assessment to Congress on the feasibility, advisability, and potential benefits to the Department of establishing the incubator programs described in Section 1071. The purpose of this information request is to ensure that any potential assessment provided to Congress and any subsequently authorized incubator program are grounded in realistic construction, security, governance, and sustainment planning. Early identification of cost, compliance, and institutional commitment factors is intended to reduce risk for both the U.S. Government and participating institutions. This RFI is for planning and assessment purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation.

description: The IF109 Framework is being established to support delivery of NI Water's capital investment programme and will succeed the existing IF105 Integrated Partnerships Framework, which is due to expire in May 2028. The Framework is intended to support delivery of the PC28 investment programme and future regulatory periods whilst securing the capacity, capability, flexibility, value for money and resilience required to deliver NI Water's future capital programme. The IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework will support a range of works and related services including programme and project management, design, engineering, construction, commissioning and other supporting or ancillary activities necessary to support the successful delivery of NI Water's capital investment programme. The Framework is intended to support delivery of NI Water's future investment priorities, including regulatory compliance, service improvement, resilience enhancement, environmental performance and long-term sustainability objectives. The IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework comprises four Lots covering: Lot 1 - Minor Civil Pipelaying Works Lot 2 - Minor Civil Works Lot 3 - Minor MEICA & Process Works Lot 4 - Major Civil, MEICA & Process Works Together, these Lots will support the delivery of projects ranging from small-scale network investment and rehabilitation activities through to large-scale, complex, multidisciplinary capital programmes across NI Water's water and wastewater asset base. The Framework has been designed to support long-term delivery of NI Water's investment programme whilst providing the flexibility required to respond to evolving programme, funding and operational requirements throughout its duration. The total framework value may be shared across all Lots.

title: Small Business D/B Military Construction MATOC
description: DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) W912QR25R0018 for the Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple-Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) pools for design-build and design-bid-build construction and renovation projects within the Louisville Districts Area of Responsibility consisting of Michigan, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and Kentucky. TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for a target of seven (7) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) MATOC contracts. Each contract will have up to a five-year ordering period with an option to extend up to six months in accordance with FAR 52.217-8. No additional capacity will be added if/when the option is exercised, as the contract capacity is for the entire life of the contract.. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be listed as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Trade Off source selection process. The technical information contained in the Offerors proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Phase I consideration will be given in two (2) evaluation factors: Past Performance and Technical Approach. The highest rated proposals will be down-selected, and offerors with these proposals will be invited to submit proposals for Phase II. A target of ten (10) most highly qualified offerors will be selected to participate in Phase II. During Phase II, consideration will be given in three (3) evaluation factors: Design/Technical, Management Approach and Price. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions. CAPACITY/CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: This MATOC will have a capacity not-to-exceed $240,000,000. The construction magnitude of the sample project is anticipated to be between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000, in accordance with FAR 36.204. SOLICITATION WEBSITE: The official solicitation, when posted, will be available free of charge by electronic posting only and may be found at the Contracting Opportunities website, https://sam.gov/. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Telephone and Fax requests for this solicitation will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. To download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at the Contracting Opportunities website at https://www.sam.gov. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the above referenced website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the website periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. REGISTRATIONS:Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database:System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective Offeror. POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contacts for this procurement is Contract Specialist, Jessica Moss, at Jessica.K.Moss@usace.army.mil.

description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL SERVICES Solicitation Number: 3930313PR270000003 Project Title: HVAC Diagnostic and Repairs at USCG Station Lake Worth Inlet Issuing Agency: United States Coast Guard (USCG) � Base Miami Beach (P&C) / CGD-SE Notice Type: Combined Synopsis / Solicitation Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside Applicable NAICS Code: 238220 � Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Acquisition Authority: FAR Subpart 12.6, FAR Part 13 (Simplified Acquisition Procedures), and FAR Part 15 1. General Notice & Acquisition Overview This document constitutes a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Sole Solicitation: This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; no separate written solicitation will be issued. Small Business Set-Aside: This procurement is advertised as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS code 238220. Basis for Award: Award will be made using simplified acquisition procedures to the responsible offeror whose proposal conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. 2. Key Procurement Schedule & Contacts Milestone / Requirement Date / Time Details / Point of Contact Organized Site Visit October 29 , 2026 @ 09:00 AM EST (Coordinate base access 48 hrs in advance) Location: USCG Station Lake Worth Inlet, 3300 Lakeshore Dr., Riviera Beach, FL 33404 Technical POC: MKC Marissa Massey Phone: 561-718-0424 Email: MARISSA.A.MASSEY@USCG.MIL Questions Deadline November 05, 2026 @ 1:00 PM EST Submit via email using the mandatory subject format below. Proposal Submission Deadline November 12, 2026 @ 1:00 PM EST Electronic submission to Contracting Officer: Ulric.Waldron@uscg.mil. Period of Performance 14 Calendar Days All assessment, repair, testing, closeout documentation, and O&M manual submissions must be completed within 14 calendar days post-award. Authorized Work Hours Mon � Fri, 0700 � 1600 (7:00 AM � 4:00 PM) Work outside these hours requires prior written approval from the Coast Guard unit command/COR. No weekend or federal holiday work authorized without prior consent. Points of Contact Contracting & Proposal Inquiries: Ulric Waldron, Contracting Officer / Contract Specialist Email: Ulric.Waldron@uscg.mil Mailing / Delivery Address: Commanding Officer USCG Base Miami Beach (P&C) Attn: Ulric Waldron 16001 SW 117th Avenue Miami, FL 33177 Technical, Scheduling Inquiries & Site Visit Access: MKC Marissa Massey Phone: 561-718-0424 Email: MARISSA.A.MASSEY@USCG.MIL 3. Place of Performance Facility: U.S. Coast Guard Station Lake Worth Inlet Building: Station Building (STA BULDG - CGD-SE) Physical Address: 3300 Lakeshore Drive Riviera Beach, FL 33404 4. Scope of Work (Summary of Specifications) 4.1 General Work Requirements The Contractor shall furnish all necessary labor, materials, equipment, transportation, and supervision to perform a comprehensive diagnostic assessment and repairs of the facility�s HVAC and cooling tower systems: Inspection & Assessment: Inspect all HVAC equipment, cooling towers, circulating pumps, piping, controls, and associated electrical/mechanical distribution assemblies. Operational Testing: Evaluate overall system condition, measure operational readings (pressures, temperatures, electrical draws, airflow), and identify functional deficiencies, component failures, and root causes of performance issues. Corrective Actions & Repairs: Execute required repairs, maintenance, component replacements, and necessary adjustments in accordance with manufacturer standards and National Electric Code (NEC). Comprehensive Summary Report: Provide a formal engineering/technical diagnostic report including detailed findings, photographic documentation, recommended follow-on corrective actions, and budgetary cost estimations. 4.2 Contractor Qualifications & Technical Standards Licensing: All installation, diagnostic, and repair work shall be performed by an HVAC contractor actively licensed and certified in the State of Florida. Code Compliance: All electrical and mechanical work shall strictly comply with the most current edition of the National Electrical Code (NEC) and applicable ASHRAE standards. Safety & Hot Work: The contractor shall comply with all Coast Guard safety regulations, including obtaining required hot work permits prior to open-flame brazing, cutting, or welding. Utilities & Facility Operations: Reasonable quantities of electricity and potable water will be made available without charge. The contractor shall furnish necessary backflow preventers, connections, and temporary facilities if required. Coordinate all staging and equipment laydown areas with the COR. 4.3 Required Submittals & Deliverables Personnel Roster: Full roster of on-site personnel submitted prior to pre-work conference (First Name, Last Name, Job Title, Company). All personnel must comply with the REAL ID Act of 2005 for base entry. Safety Program Plan: Outlining accident prevention, fall protection, and site-specific hazard mitigation. Project Schedule: Work progression schedule showing milestones within the 14-calendar-day performance period. Product Data Sheets: Technical catalog cuts and manufacturer specifications for any replaced components. Operation & Maintenance (O&M) Manuals & Training: Electronic submittal containing warranty details, parts list, test data, startup/shutdown sequence, and provision of operational training to designated station personnel prior to final acceptance. 5. Proposal Submission Instructions 5.1 Submission Methods & Protocols Electronic Submission (Preferred): Deliver via email in PDF format to Ulric.Waldron@uscg.mil. Telephone or verbal quotes will not be considered. Mailing / Hand Delivery: Must arrive at USCG Base Miami Beach (P&C), Attn: Ulric Waldron, 16001 SW 117th Avenue, Miami, FL 33177 prior to the closing deadline. Amendments: Formal solicitation amendments and Q&A notices will be publicized via SAM.gov. 5.2 Mandatory Email Subject Formatting All email communications must use the exact subject lines below: Proposal Submission: [PROPOSAL SUBMISSION] [3930313PR270000003] - [USCG Station Lake Worth Inlet HVAC Diagnostic & Repair] ([Company Name]) Question / Clarification Submission: [QUESTION SUBMISSION] [3930313PR270000003] - [USCG Station Lake Worth Inlet HVAC Diagnostic & Repair] ([Company Name]) 5.3 Administrative & Technical Proposal Requirements Offerors must include the following documentation in their proposal package: Entity Identifiers: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN/EIN), and CAGE Code. Active SAM.gov Registration: Active registration with representations and certifications completed prior to award. State of Florida HVAC License: Proof of active State of Florida Certified HVAC Contractor licensing. Technical Capability Statement: Brief description of proposed methodology to complete the assessment, repairs, and deliverables within the 14-calendar-day performance window. Past Performance: Minimum of two (2) recent, relevant commercial or government marine/industrial HVAC projects. Price Proposal: Complete firm-fixed-price breakdown (Labor, Materials, Diagnostics/Reporting, and Total Proposed FFP). 6. Evaluation and Basis for Award Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quote represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Proposals will be evaluated under the following factors: Factor 1 � Technical Acceptability: Demonstrated capability to execute all requirements in Section 01 11 00. title: Small Business D/B Military Construction MATOC
description: DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) W912QR25R0018 for the Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple-Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) pools for design-build and design-bid-build construction and renovation projects within the Louisville Districts Area of Responsibility consisting of Michigan, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and Kentucky. TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for a target of seven (7) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) MATOC contracts. Each contract will have up to a five-year ordering period with an option to extend up to six months in accordance with FAR 52.217-8. No additional capacity will be added if/when the option is exercised, as the contract capacity is for the entire life of the contract.. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be listed as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Trade Off source selection process. The technical information contained in the Offerors proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Phase I consideration will be given in two (2) evaluation factors: Past Performance and Technical Approach. The highest rated proposals will be down-selected, and offerors with these proposals will be invited to submit proposals for Phase II. A target of ten (10) most highly qualified offerors will be selected to participate in Phase II. During Phase II, consideration will be given in three (3) evaluation factors: Design/Technical, Management Approach and Price. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions. CAPACITY/CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: This MATOC will have a capacity not-to-exceed $240,000,000. The construction magnitude of the sample project is anticipated to be between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000, in accordance with FAR 36.204. SOLICITATION WEBSITE: The official solicitation, when posted, will be available free of charge by electronic posting only and may be found at the Contracting Opportunities website, https://sam.gov/. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Telephone and Fax requests for this solicitation will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. To download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at the Contracting Opportunities website at https://www.sam.gov. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the above referenced website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the website periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. REGISTRATIONS:Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database:System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective Offeror. POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contacts for this procurement is Contract Specialist, Jessica Moss, at Jessica.K.Moss@usace.army.mil.

description: FA860127R0010 Amendment 0001:-Update SOW section 45.1 with new email for Ombudsman - Remove Clause 52.216-32, Task Order and Delivery Order Ombudsman - Add Clause 52.228-1, Bid Guarantee - The solicitation number changed from FA860126R0017 to FA860127R0010 due to entering the new fiscal year. The solicitation number then changed from FA860127R0010 to FA860127R00100001 due to amendment 1.Initial Solicitation FA860126R0017: The United States Air Force, AFLCMC/Operational Contracting Branch, Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio is seeking industry proposals. This acquisition is full and open to all contractors and will provide the inspection, diagnostics, and renewal of both low- and medium-voltage electrical systems. This may require modernization or replacement of transformers, switchgear, panelboards, protective devices, motor control centers, emergency generator assemblies with transfer switches, fire alarm networks, power conditioning equipment, surge and lightning protection, interior and specialty lighting systems, conductors, cables, and associated terminations. Additional requirements may involve repair and integration of Direct Digital Controls (DDC) for HVAC, vertical transportation equipment control/lighting systems, and other specialized building automation systems. Additionally, work may extend to overhead and underground distribution systems, service feeders, grounding grids, duct banks, conduit networks, and manholes. The prime contractor will be expected to provide temporary power during outages, coordinate system cutovers, and perform functional testing, commissioning, and acceptance activities to verify compliance with all current codes and Wright Patterson AFB Installation Facility Standards. Energy efficiency-driven upgrades, and emergency repair services may also be executed under this contract.

description: ****Amend 0002 posted 20260902: Provide specifics for the site visit****Amend 0001 posted 20260817: Provide correct Plans Room Key****VA Hospital Solicitation Notice W912DQ26RA060. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. Offerors shall submit an offer subject to Project Labor Agreement (PLA) requirements in accordance with RFO 22.5, Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Any PLA reached pursuant to the PLA requirements in the solicitation does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government. Funds are fully available for this requirement. The project will be solicited as full and open (unrestricted). The requirements under this construction project include right sizing the VAs medical center by demolishing several deficient and underutilized buildings and then constructing multiple new modern and seismically compliant structures and facilities on the same, expanded site. The newly constructed facilities are incorporated into a master plan for future expansion and demolition of additional primary facilities. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a small business size standard of $45 million in average annual receipts. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. The estimated performance period for the pre-construction services phase is 820 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).Interested offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). If the offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity must have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. A Proposal Guarantee will be required with your proposal in the amount of 20% of the Offerors proposed price or $3,000,000, whichever is less. Payment and Performance Bonds will be required for the full amount (100%) of the awarded contract before the Notice to Proceed can be issued. Point of Contact: The point of contact for all questions/inquiries is Michael France at michael.g.france@usace.army.mil and David Walsh (Contracting Officer) at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil.

description: 21-Oct-2026: Posting Amendment 0002. Extending the offer due date to 12 Nov 2026, 10:00 AM HST. Additional answers once received to questions related to the plans and specifications will be incorporated in a future amendment. ____07-Oct-2026: Posting Amendment 0001, preproposal conference slides and sign-in attendance sheet in PIEE/Solicitation Module. The purpose of Amendment 0001 is to change Questions due NLT 16 Oct 2026, 5:00 PM HST, and the offer due date to 30 Oct 2026, 3:30 PM HST. ____23-Sep-2026: This is a Solicitation Notice, Request for Proposal. Single Project RFP Set-Aside for Small Businesses NAICS Code: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Hawaii National Guard intends to issue a Request for Proposals (RFP) to award a single firm fixed-price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances and supervision necessary for the Construction of KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection Facility and KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition located on the Hawaii Air National Guard campus, at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH), Hawaii. These projects will be concurrent. KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection Facility - Construct a new Munitions Maintenance and Inspections facility by utilizing conventional design and construction methods to accommodate the facility mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project - Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC Section 2805. Project square footage is estimated at 2,400 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Micro-pile Foundations: Specialized foundation engineering featuring micro-piles to mitigate challenging soil conditions and ensure seismic structural integrity. Cast-in-Place Concrete: Constructing robust concrete slab-on-grade, concrete walls, capping beams, and associated structural masonry elements. Structural Framing and Enclosure: Utilizing cold-formed metal framing, insulated metal wall panels, and structural steel support systems. Roofing: Installation of high-performance standing seam metal roofing, complete with prefinished gutters, downspouts, and weather barrier wraps. Specialized Systems: Installation of mechanical HVAC systems (including specialized 20-ton air conditioning systems), interior plumbing, lightning/grounding protection, and communication infrastructure. Fire Protection: A complete fire alarm-mass notification system and wet-pipe sprinkler suppression system. In addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following option line items: 1. MAC Pad - Construct 1,167 SY concrete pad for the Material Assembly Center (MAC), required for constructing munitions, along with new asphalt pavement for access and egress to the facility maintenance bays. KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition - Construct an addition to the Munitions Cube Storage Facility (B3552) utilizing conventional design and construction methods to support the F-22 mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project - Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC Section 2805. Project square footage is estimated at 1,320 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Substructure and Enclosure: Micro-pile foundations, concrete wall structures, cast-in-place concrete slabs, and 12 in. thick concrete walls designed for high-hazard storage specifications. Framing and Roofing: Structural steel framing, roof joists, and standing seam metal roofing matching existing facility standards. Exterior Elements: Erection of new asphalt pavement adjacent to the existing facility access to provide adequate logistics and material handling access around the new facility addition. Specialized Protection: Maintenance facility lightning and grounding protection systems, along with integrated fire detection and alarm reporting systems connected back to the base reporting system. APPLICABLE TO BOTH PROJECTS: RAB Lighting exterior wall packs and area lights are sole source/brand name specific for compatibility with existing installation systems (noted justifications will be included with solicitation). Project Phasing and Security Gates: The contractor will be required to erect a temporary security fence around the construction zone in accordance with the project staging and phasing drawings. Escort Requirements: Escort personnel shall be required when erecting the temporary security fence, performing work occurring outside the temporary security fence, and connecting utilities to the existing system. Secured Zone Access: Once the temporary security fencing is approved and accepted by the Contracting Officers Representative (COR), no escort shall be required within the active secured work zone during construction, allowing the contractor to work within the secured boundary unimpeded. The magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000 total. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. Offerors shall submit an offer subject to Project Labor Agreement (PLA) requirements in accordance with RFO 22.5, Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Any PLA reached pursuant to the PLA requirements in the solicitation does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government. Funds are fully available for this requirement. The project will be solicited as full and open (unrestricted). The requirements under this construction project include right sizing the VAs medical center by demolishing several deficient and underutilized buildings and then constructing multiple new modern and seismically compliant structures and facilities on the same, expanded site. The newly constructed facilities are incorporated into a master plan for future expansion and demolition of additional primary facilities. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a small business size standard of $45 million in average annual receipts. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. The estimated performance period for the pre-construction services phase is 820 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).Interested offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). title: F-15EX Missile Warning System
description: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Fighters & Advanced Aircraft Directorate (AFLCMC/WA), F?15 System Program Office (AFLCMC/WAQ), Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB) is seeking sources for the procurement of an operationally qualified threat missile launch and approach warning system for rapid integration into the United States Air Force (USAF) F-15EX Eagle II fighter aircraft. INTRODUCTION: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT to acquire a missile warning system (MWS) to be integrated into the F-15EX fleet. The system must alert the F-15EX aircrew to missile threats without unreasonably distracting the aircrew with false alarms. The MWS must use the six pre-existing sensor locations, data cables, power cables, and cooling. The MWS must be easily, safely, rapidly, and organically installable and removable in the field by USAF military aircraft maintenance personnel. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 10, Market Research, AFLCMC/WAQ is seeking information for potential sources for an integrated MWS solution for the F-15EX. This publication is intended to elicit responses from sources with knowledge, skills, data, equipment, access to appropriate facilities, and the capacity to meet the Air Force�s requirements. The dollar value and period of performance (PoP) for the contract will be commensurate with the requirement. This contract effort is subject to RFO 52.232-18, Availability of Funds. 1.1 SOURCES SOUGHT INFORMATION 1.2 DISCLAIMER: THIS?SOURCES SOUGHT?IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY.? THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB).?IN ACCORDANCE WITH?RFO 15.101(c),?THIS NOTICE?DOES NOT CONSTITUTE SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. THE GOVERNMENT MAY USE THE INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE IN DETERMINING ITS ACQUISITION APPROACH.? THE ISSUANCE OF THIS NOTICE DOES NOT RESTRICT THE GOVERNMENT ACQUISTION APPROACH.? 1.3 REQUIRED CAPABILITIES Interested firms should submit information as to the capabilities, capacity, and experience to provide an MWS as set forth below: The MWS must alert the F-15EX aircrew to the presence of missiles that may threaten the aircraft without unreasonably distracting the aircrew with false alarms. The MWS must use the six (6) pre-existing F-15EX sensor locations, data cables, power cables, and cooling. It must be easily, safely, rapidly, and organically installable and removable in the field by USAF military aircraft maintenance personnel without requiring any change to aircraft configuration beyond installation of MWS line replaceable units (LRUs) in the six (6) pre-existing locations in the aircraft dedicated for missile warning. To avoid compromise of classified information, this notice does not ask for threat missile launch and approach detection performance for various use cases nor for an MWS concept of operations. AFLCMC/WAQ may contact you to ask for detection performance information if your response to this Sources Sought notice indicates your MWS is integrable in an F-15EX aircraft. Questions: What is the name of the MWS you describe in your response to this Sources Sought notice? Please include titles, abbreviations, and nomenclature as available. Please only identify and describe a single MWS in your response. On what Department of War (DoW) aircraft model(s) is your MWS approved for operational use today? Approval for operational use requires both 1) determination of airworthiness of the aircraft with your MWS integrated and 2) sustainment of the aircraft�s cybersecurity Authorization to Operate. Who are the best references (name, position, organization, commercial telephone number, and US Government email address) for DoW acquirers responsible for procuring your MWS for operational use on DoW aircraft named in question 2? Is your MWS in active production today? How many months from contract award could your MWS be delivered? Does your MWS consist only of sensor LRUs or does your MWS consist of sensor LRUs connected to a central processing LRU? If MWS sensors are connected to a central processor, how are they connected? What are the dimensions of each LRU in your MWS? You are alternately welcome to include in your response figures from engineering drawings that identify dimensions, rather than listing dimensions. How much does each LRU in your MWS weigh? How are your MWS�s LRUs physically fastened to an aircraft? What are your MWS�s electrical power requirements? Through what cable connection(s) is your MWS powered by the aircraft? What are your MWS�s cooling requirements? Through what interface(s) is your MWS cooled by the aircraft? Can your MWS be connected to an aircraft�s MIL-STD-1553 avionics bus? What are the terms by which your firm will share the MIL-STD-1553 avionics bus interface specification for your MWS with The Boeing Company so data can be exchanged between your MWS and the F-15EX�s onboard mission computer? Does your MWS require the aircrew or maintenance personnel to provide information to your MWS during aircraft preflight or midflight for it to correctly detect missiles that may threaten the aircraft? If so, how is this information provided to your MWS? Does the installation on, operation of, or removal of your MWS from an aircraft expose personnel to a known health or safety hazard? Are there any known limitations on your MWS�s use in the F-15EX aircraft�s operational environment as verified in accordance with MIL-STD-810H? title: MODIFIED WC-130J RTP APN-241 WEATHER RADAR SUSTAINING ENGINEERING SUPPORT RESEARCH AND SUPPORT TASK
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualifications to support repairability maintainability, and sustaining engineering for the modified WC-130J RTP APN-241 Weather Radar. Potential sources must possess the ability to provide engineering studies for the WC-130J RTP APN-241 system in resolving reliability and maintainability issues, obsolete parts issues, identify and propose solutions to Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) issues, and analyze failure trends from both the depots and the field level shops to support the MC-130J CR-2M developmental testing. For vendors wishing to participate in this Request for Information (RFI), after reviewing the requirement, provide documentation supporting proof of company�s capability to meet the requested requirements. If lacking sufficient experience/capabilities in a particular area, please provide details explaining strategies to overcome the lack of experience/capabilities to perform that portion of the requirement. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), this RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or services. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses incurred in response to this RFI; all cost associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in future RFPs nor does it ensure participation, if an RFP is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Federal Business Opportunities (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Potential sources must be able to install the APN-241 Weather radar in addition to troubleshooting system discrepancies. Potential sources must be capable of and have access to Northrop Grumman equipment. description: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Fighters & Advanced Aircraft Directorate (AFLCMC/WA), F?15 System Program Office (AFLCMC/WAQ), Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB) is seeking sources for the procurement of an operationally qualified threat missile launch and approach warning system for rapid integration into the United States Air Force (USAF) F-15EX Eagle II fighter aircraft. title: Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) Laboratory Testing
description: In Cooperation with Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) SECTION 1 - Overview 1.1 Background and Introduction Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) is seeking laboratories to validate the capabilities of Individual Water Treatment Devices (IWTDs). This initiative supports the Department of the Army�s goal of providing potable drinking water for Soldiers from any indigenous fresh water source, which enhances Soldier lethality by reducing load and increasing the duration of autonomous squad-level operations. The Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on behalf of PdM SCIE, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify laboratories with the required certifications, equipment, and personnel to conduct this validation testing. The information gathered from this RFI will inform a future request for proposal. The Government reserves the right to cancel this opportunity or make no awards in conjunction with this opportunity. This is a Request for Information ONLY and not a request for proposal. 1.2 Project Problem Statement The objective of this effort is to validate the ability of Individual Water Treatment Devices (IWTD) to perform clearance of microbiological contaminants and Toxic Industrial Chemicals/Toxic Industrial Materials (TIC/TIMs). Testing must be conducted according to the military-specific purification standards outlined in National Sanitation Foundation (NSF) Protocols P248.01 and P248.02. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to, the following laboratory capabilities: Certification to ISO 17025:2017 or equivalent. Ability to evaluate devices against NSF P248.01 and/or P248.02 protocols. Capability to draft product-specific test plans in accordance with the P248 validation scheme. Commitment to provide all raw data, test data, and internal standard data. SECTION 2 - RFI Procedures This RFI is seeking information from qualified sources that can address the stated requirements. All responses to this announcement will be governed by the instructions herein. Interested parties are requested to submit information packages that present their planned approach to addressing the testing objectives. Packages should focus on the laboratory�s technical approach, capabilities, and relevant experience. SECTION 3 - Instructions for Information Submissions 3.1 General Guidelines a. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures are not desired. b. All submissions must be submitted electronically via the email instructions included herein. c. Submissions sent through other channels or after the response period has ended will not be reviewed or evaluated. d. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs will be at the expense of the interested party. 3.2 Information Package Contents Interested parties shall include the following information in their response: A statement confirming if the laboratory is certified to ISO 17025:2017 or equivalent. A statement confirming if the laboratory is equipped to evaluate devices against NSF P248.01 and/or P248.02 protocols. If subletting work to another laboratory, provide name, credentials and last audit of that laboratory An estimated timeline for executing the validation testing, assuming an award in Nov/Dec 2026. Information regarding the firm's experience, personnel, and facilities. Supporting technical information (e.g., technical literature, test data, illustrations). Company background, business size (including socioeconomic status), CAGE code, and applicable NAICS code. GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract number, if applicable. 3.3 Information Package Submission Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to the following points of contact (POCs): Eric Brack, eric.m.brack.civ@army.mil Parker Brandwein, parker.d.brandwein.civ@army.mil Blaise Liess, blaise.p.liess.civ@army.mil Ronda Hinnant, ronda.r.hinnant.civ@army.mil Responses shall be submitted no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Responses received after this time and date may not be considered. The subject line for responses shall read: �Response to IWTD Laboratory Testing RFI, [Vendor�s Business Name]� SECTION 5 - Government Points of Contact Any questions for clarification regarding this opportunity may be emailed to the POCs listed below no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will not be accepted. Questions shall not contain proprietary or classified information. title: Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT)
description: SYNOPSIS: #N68335-26-Q-1204 Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT) Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division - F/A-18F and EA-18G Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Program The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Hydraulics International, Inc. (CAGE: 56529) for the Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT) in support of the NAWCAD F/A-18F and EA-18G Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Program. This order will procure one (1) APCLT (Part Number (P/N): 4129AS0100-1, National Stock Number (NSN): 4920-01-658-2036). The APCLT is required to check aircraft pressurized cabins and canopy seals for leaks and for the ability to control aircraft cabin pressure. The pneumatic cabin pressure leakage tester will provide the means to meet the requirement and is required by the RAAF. The pneumatic cabin pressure leakage tester is a portable unit that runs on facility supplied compressed air and that can supply various combinations of air flow and air pressure to check leakage and pressure regulation in aircraft cabins and canopy seals. Hydraulics International, Inc., as the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the APCLT, is the only source with the requisite knowledge, technical experience, and production-level data to produce these components. The components being procured are integral to check aircraft pressurized cabins and canopy seals for leaks and for the ability to control aircraft cabin pressure and are critical to maintaining operational readiness. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), FAR 6.302-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, the Government will consider all responses received within fifteen days after the date of publication of this synopsis. Registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) is mandatory for consideration. A determination by the Government not to open the requirement to competition based on the responses to this notice will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for an award of a contract. title: Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) for Reduction/Removal of Toxic Industrial Chemicals and Materials
description: In Cooperation with Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) and the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Soldier Center SECTION 1 - Overview 1.1 Background and Introduction The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Soldier Center is conducting a market investigation to identify products and technologies for individual Soldier water purification. This effort focuses on capabilities for the reduction or removal of Toxic Industrial Chemicals (TICs) and Toxic Industrial Materials (TIMs) from any indigenous fresh water sources. This Request for Information (RFI) seeks to identify suppliers of water treatment technologies that meet Buy American Act requirements and can be integrated with current and future equipment, such as the Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) and MOLLE Hydration System. Information gathered will be used for planning purposes to address military water purification needs. Respondents are encouraged to submit alternative technical approaches or product solutions that vary from the listed specifications, as long as they meet or exceed the core capability requirement. This is a Sources Sought Announcement for information and planning purposes only. It is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) and does not constitute a commitment by the U.S. Government. 1.2 Project Problem Statement The DEVCOM Soldier Center is interested in products and technologies that meet or have the potential to meet the following key performance parameters for individual water purification. Respondents should provide actual, demonstrated product performance for each parameter, including where performance does not meet specifications listed below: Contaminant Removal: Capable of removing TICs and TIMs to levels mandated by the Defense Health Agency (DCPH-A), as detailed in the attached "Toxic Industrial Chemical/Material Military Exposure Guideline." Compatibility: Compatible with standard military canteens and hydration systems. Physical Specifications: Weight: Not to exceed 12 oz. Size: Low bulk and compact. Operational Life: At least 135 liters. Shelf Life: 5-year storage stability with an 18-month unused service life. Environmental Resilience: System will not degrade in temperatures from -33�C to 52�C. Capable of treating water ranging in temperature from above freezing to 52�C (liquid water up to 52�C). Must not be impacted by freezing and remain functional upon thawing. Fully functional in all operational environments. Performance: Treat-to-Drink Time: Ideally less than 5 minutes (target less than 20 minutes). Flow Rate: Not less than 200 mL/min (if applicable). Water Quality: Processed water must be palatable, similar to commercial bottled water. Ease of use with or without gloved hands. Power: Batteries, if used, must be a commercially available type. Microbiological Mitigation: Ideally meets or exceeds requirements of NSF Protocol P248.01 (optional). SECTION 2 - RFI Procedures This RFI is issued to identify interested sources and gather information on market capabilities. Participation is voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with responding. Failure to respond does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. SECTION 3 - Instructions for Information Submissions 3.1 General Guidelines a. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures are not desired. b. Submissions must be sent electronically via email as instructed below. c. The Government will not pay for any information, administrative costs, or product samples submitted in response to this notice. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 3.2 Information Package Contents Interested parties are invited to submit responses detailing their products, technologies, and capabilities. The submission should include: A description of current commercial product(s) and how they can address the military requirements. Technical information (e.g., technical literature, test data, patents, illustrations). Information regarding the firm's experience, personnel, and facilities. Product cost information. Company information: business size (including socioeconomic status), CAGE code, and applicable NAICS code. GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract number, if applicable. A physical sample (optional; no payment will be made for unsolicited samples). Any relevant data on microbiological or chemical reductions. 3.3 Information Package Submission Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to the following points of contact (POCs): Eric Brack, eric.m.brack.civ@army.mil Parker Brandwein, parker.d.brandwein.civ@army.mil Blaise Liess, blaise.p.liess.civ@army.mil Ronda Hinnant, ronda.r.hinnant.civ@army.mil Responses must be submitted no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Responses received after this time may not be considered. The subject line shall read: �Response to IWTD TIC/TIM RFI, [Vendor�s Business Name]� SECTION 5 - Government Points of Contact Any questions for clarification may be emailed to the POCs listed below no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will not be accepted. title: Denmark – Industrial machinery – Delivery and installation of a ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics
description: DTU Nanolab wishes to acquire a high ion density source reactive ion etcher for oxides and nitrides of silicon to become its new primary instrument for 150 mm wafer processing. Delivery is expected no later than Q3 2027. The Instrument will be installed in the DTU Nanolab cleanroom - a university facility providing a comprehensive suite of micro- and nanofabrication tools. It serves a diverse community of over 200 active users, ranging from novice students to experienced researchers, as well a high percentage of commercial clients. As an open access tool, the Instrument must support the full spectrum of etching of silicon-based dielectrics, from sub 100 nm nanostructures defined by electron beam lithography to depths of several tens of microns. Meeting these demands requires exceptional process controllability and tunability: the system must perform ultra precise, low-rate etches (< 100 nm/min) with smooth and straight sidewalls and minimal undercut for shallow features, alongside high etch rate deep etches (approaching 500 nm/min). It must also accommodate all silicon dielectrics of the form SixNy, SixOx and SixOyNz, and be compatible with mask materials including Si, Cr, e-beam resists and UV/DUV photoresists with high mask selectivity for all these masking materials. The user interface must be intuitive and user friendly. The Instrument should be engineered to the highest industrial standards to minimize maintenance, and any required servicing must be straightforward and efficient. The instrument must be configured for 150 mm wafer processing and a complete kit enabling the processing of 200 mm wafers must be included in the tender as an option. Furthermore, DTU will have the option to purchase one more ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics identical to the initial instrument.

At its plenary meeting in December 2025, the tripartite Advisory Committee on Safety and Health at Work (ACSH) adopted an opinion on the state of play and future impulses regarding the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work4. Moreover, in June 2026, the Commission adopted the Report on the screening of the EU acquis in the area of health and safety at work5, and its accompanying Staff Working Document6 [TBC]. The results of this screening exercise study will inform the process of developing new EU OSH priorities in the strategic framework on health and safety at work after 2027.

title: Germany – Agricultural services – Beratung landwirtschaftlicher Betriebe zur Erhaltung und Verbesserung der Biodiversität und Nachhaltigkeit in der Landwirtschaft (EB)
description: Für das ML soll eine Rahmenvereinbarung zur Erbringung von Beratungsdienstleistungen nach Art. 78 der EU Strategieplan VO (EU) 2021/2115 vom 2. Dezember 2021 vergeben werden. Ausgeschrieben werden definierte Beratungsdienstleistungen für landwirtschaftliche Betriebe. Die Maßnahme zielt auf die Erhaltung und Verbesserung der Nachhaltigkeit landwirtschaftlicher Betriebe unter besonderer Beachtung der Aspekte der Biodiversität, der Klimaresilienz, des Tierwohls und eines effizienten Umgangs mit Ressourcen durch Wissenstransfer. Die Beratungsleistungen sind nur dann förderfähig, wenn die Beratungen durch nach diesem Vergabeverfahren ausgewählte Beratungsanbieter und Beratungskräfte durchgeführt werden. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind der Leistungsbeschreibung - Fachlicher Teil (Teil B) und der Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C) - sowie den weiteren beigefügten Anlagen zu entnehmen. Die Rahmenvereinbarung soll mit mehreren Unternehmen (§ 21 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 VgV) abgeschlossen werden, um den Landwirten eine Wahl des Beratungsanbieters zu ermöglichen. Dabei werden so viele Zuschläge entsprechend der Platzierung nach der Angebotswertung erteilt, bis die Angebotssummen der bezuschlagten Angebote die zur Verfügung stehende Fördersumme von 5.849.200 EUR im Vertragszeitraum 01. März 2027 - 30. Juni 2029 erreicht ist. Das zuletzt bezuschlagte Angebot wird daher voraussichtlich nicht in vollem Umfang berücksichtigt werden können, sondern nur insoweit bis die zur Verfügung stehenden Fördermittel ausgeschöpft sind. Das maximal mögliche Mittelvolumen je Beratungsanbieter in dem gesamten Vertragszeitraum wird im Rahmen des Vergabeverfahrens ermittelt, wobei je Beratungsanbieter maximal ein Betrag in Höhe von bis zu 300.000 EUR zugeteilt wird. Dieser Betrag kann im Fall einer späteren Zuteilung von gestrichenen Mitteln (s.u.) überschritten werden. Für den Fall, dass ein Beratungsanbieter seinen Betrag nicht benötigt/abruft, werden ihm Mittel gestrichen. Die dann frei gewordenen Mittel können an die anderen Beratungsanbieter zugewiesen werden. Weitere Einzelheiten hierzu finden sich in der Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C). Der Abschluss der Rahmenvereinbarung bildet zunächst keinen Anspruch auf die Mittel und stellt keine Erteilung einer Zuwendung dar. Hierfür muss im Rahmen des Zuwendungsverfahrens ein separater Förderantrag gestellt und dieser bewilligt werden (siehe hierzu auch Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C)).

title: Germany – Landscaping work – Stiftung Schloss Marienburg: Bauabschnitt 2: Garten- und Landschaftsbau: Oberbauschichten
description: Die Stiftung Schloss Marienburg beabsichtigt die Sanierung des Schlosses. Das Gebäude ist ein eingetragenes Baudenkmal. Die historische Bausubstanz ist zu schonen und zu erhalten. Die Erfordernisse aus dem Denkmalschutz verlangen von allen am Bau beteiligten Firmen eine besondere Vorsicht und Sorgfalt und eine enge Abstimmung mit der Bauleitung. Sanierung des Schlosses Marienburg, Bauabschnitte 2.1 Hangsicherung und 2.2 Terrasse Süd - Garten- und Landschaftsbauarbeiten zur Herstellung von Oberbauschichten, Pflasterbelägen und Entwässerungsanlagen. Die Leistungen umfassen insbesondere Erdarbeiten, Herstellung von Bodenaufbauten, Ziegelpflaster und wassergebundenen Wegedecken, Abdichtungs- und Dränagearbeiten, Entwässerungsleitungen und -rinnen sowie Entsorgung und Dokumentation. Der zu sanierende Hangbereich besteht aus einer bis zu rund 13 m hohen und bis zu rund 65° gegenüber der Horizontalen geneigten Festgesteinswand aus Buntsandstein. Im oberen Bereich des Hanges befindet sich ein historischer Laubengang, der mittels einer Gewölbekonstruktion auf dem Hang aufgelagert ist. Aufgrund von eindringendem Wasser und Bewuchs haben sich Teile der Felsoberfläche gelöst, wodurch die Auflagerpunkte der tragenden Konsolsteine teilweise nicht mehr vorhanden sind. Der Laubengang wird derzeit durch eine Stahlkonstruktion notabgestützt und ist gesperrt. Im Rahmen der Sanierung wird der Bodenaufbau des Laubengangs einschließlich Pflasterbelag, Abdichtung und Entwässerung erneuert. Im Bauabschnitt 2.2 ist die Nutzbarmachung der Terrasse Süd vorgesehen. Hierzu wird die vorhandene Betonoberfläche zurückgebaut und ein neuer Bodenaufbau mit wassergebundener Wegedecke hergestellt. Bestandteil der Maßnahmen ist außerdem die Erneuerung der Entwässerung sowie die Herstellung der erforderlichen Oberbauschichten auf den Stahlbetondecken. Die Arbeiten erfolgen unter besonderer Berücksichtigung des Denkmalschutzes und der historischen Bausubstanz.
